findings.title: docs_build_skipped now fails, instead of skipping, a local docs build during an open docs round whose files are uncommitted after HEAD moved — wider than the :disabled defect it fixed
findings.why_it_matters: Reproduced on a git-initialised fixture copy, with CI unset. An open check-docs round is committed at its opening head; a later fix is committed, moving HEAD; the round directory is left untracked. docs_build_skipped(cfg, 1) returns ["2026-09-09-check-docs-01"] at base (the build skips, exit 0) and String[] at head (gate_or_skip's check() throws, so the build fails). This is the normal mid-round state. The tool's own repository is in it right now: 2026-09-11-check-docs-02 has ROUND.toml modified and pass-3 untracked at HEAD 249b795. On the repo, gate_problems(cfg, "check-docs") returns [:open, :committed] and docs_build_skipped(cfg, 1) = String[]. So `julia --project=docs docs/make.jl` — which the working agreements run unasked to gate commits — goes from a skip to a red build during every docs round, until the round files are committed. Under CI (CI=true) the :committed kind is never produced and base and head agree (scenario C). The defect named in the test comment is ext#4: an open round of a DISABLED instrument swallowed by the skip. That needed only :disabled excluded. The added test exercises :disabled alone, so the :committed direction is an untested behaviour change. The makedocs docstring (DocLints.jl:22-24, unchanged) still promises a skip whenever 'either gate refus[es] only because a docs round is open'.
findings.description: The fix switched the skip test from 'any exit-1 refusal while a docs round is open' to 'every gate_problems entry is :open'. That excludes both :disabled (the reported defect) and :committed (never mentioned as a defect). The second exclusion changes the outcome of a previously valid local docs build mid-round.
findings.evidence:
BASE | B HEAD moved, round untracked, local: docs_build_skipped(cfg,1) => ["2026-09-09-check-docs-01"]
HEAD | B HEAD moved, round untracked, local: docs_build_skipped(cfg,1) => String[]
HEAD | B gate_problems => (false, [:open => "...is open (check-docs)...", :committed => "...its files are untracked or modified while HEAD moved past the round's opening head..."])
Repo at head: docs_build_skipped(cfg, 1) = String[]; frozen_rounds(cfg, docs) = ["2026-09-11-check-docs-02"]

findings.why_it_matters: Recomputing prose_units at head and comparing with the BASE CSV gives 25 units that GREW (words, longest paragraph or both). SCAN.PROSE_SHAPE reports each one as 'GREW ... rewrite, do not append; re-baseline deliberately if the growth is new content'. Four are ARCHITECTURE page units, which the 120-word cap does not bind: 'a baselined page section is held by the ratchet alone'. For those, the re-baseline removes the only guard. D10's longest paragraph went 333→379 and §6.4 went 279→294. The re-baseline is faithful: head CSV against recomputed units gives 0 mismatches, 2 keys added and 0 removed. Every docstring stays under the 120-word cap. So this records no false numbers, but the oracle moved with the change it would have flagged. No row states which growth was judged new content rather than appended prose.
findings.description: The prose-shape ratchet baseline was regenerated in the window that grew the prose. Each silenced row is a place where the ratchet's 'rewrite, do not append' was waived without a per-row record.

findings.title: ScanResult/report DEAD contract narrowed to match the code: a zero-population scan with a ledger-exempted hit is now declared not DEAD
findings.before:
- `population` — ...; zero means
  the scan measured nothing and is DEAD.
...
A scan whose population is zero measured nothing and is DEAD whatever else it did — that refusal is
the point of the counter.
findings.after:
- `population` — ...; zero, with
  no hit removed by the ledger, means the scan measured nothing and is DEAD.
...
A scan whose population is zero and from which the ledger removed no hit measured nothing and is DEAD
whatever else it did — that refusal is the point of the counter; a zero-population scan the ledger
exempted is accounted for by the ledger and is not DEAD.
findings.why_it_matters: Measured: report([ScanResult(..., hits = [], population = 0, exempted = 1, ...)]) returns 0, and with exempted = 0 it returns 2. The same predicate `dead(r) = r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0` is at base Scan.jl:457, so behaviour did not change in this window. What changed is the promise. Base said zero population is DEAD 'whatever else it did'; head licenses the exemption escape. The next sentence was kept: 'a scan that measured nothing yet hit something is a scan whose own counter is wrong'. A ledger-exempted hit is still a hit, so head now calls a scan with a demonstrably wrong counter 'accounted for' rather than DEAD. The contract was rewritten to fit the code instead of the reverse.
findings.description: The public DEAD guarantee of ScanResult and report was weakened in prose to admit a code path that contradicts the base contract. The retained next sentence now contradicts it.
findings.evidence: pop0 exempted1 -> 0; pop0 exempted0 -> 2; base: e21e57f:src/Scan.jl:457:    dead(r) = r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0

findings.title: TestHarness.resolve_function docstring's new example `Ledger.read` does not hold when Config is also in `modules`
findings.before:
A package module that OWNS the name is searched before anything else, so `Config.read`, `Git.run` and
`Scan.report` denote the package's function and not the `Base` export they collide with
findings.after:
A package module that OWNS the name is searched before anything else, so `Config.read`, `Git.run` and
`Ledger.read` denote the package's function and not the `Base` export they collide with
findings.why_it_matters: The swap was warranted: isdefined(Base, :report) = false, so `Scan.report` collided with nothing. But resolve_function takes a bare symbol. Measured: resolve_function(:read, G, [G, Config, Ledger]) returns Config.read; Ledger.read comes back only when Config is left out of `modules`. The new example promises a lookup the function cannot perform, since `:read` cannot denote both Config.read and Ledger.read.
findings.description: The docstring fix replaced a wrong example with one that is only half-right: the lookup is by bare name, and the first owning module listed wins.
findings.evidence: resolve_function(:read, G, [G, Config, Ledger]) = read owned by GBGCodingTools.Config; resolve_function(:read, G, [G, Ledger]) = read owned by GBGCodingTools.Ledger; isdefined(Base, :report) = false
